role: freeze manifest — the file list the round-77 freeze commit must carry, digest-pinned, plus the LEGCOUNT rule that binds the frozen legs[] lists to the counters' own leg tables
spec_source: wave-1 seat prompt (BUILD freeze manifest) — the 18-file core, quoted verbatim in core_files_spec below

digest.rule: sha256 over the file's committed blob content at the freeze commit — `git -C <lane> show <freeze>:<path> | sha256sum` — never over a re-serialization and never over a worktree file whose bytes differ from the blob
digest.record: manifest-check.py --root <lane> --record  (fills the placeholders from the worktree bytes about to be committed)
digest.verify: manifest-check.py --root <lane> --freeze <freeze-commit>  (reads the blobs back; a worktree/commit divergence is a MISMATCH blocker)
digest.precedent: round-76 counters pin the by-document map the same way (accept-c.py FROZENCFG: `git show <freeze>:<map.path>` whose sha256 must equal map.sha256), so the freeze blob, not the worktree, is the authority

files.why: both counters read the claim predicates, row_set, thresholds, base and legs[] from this blob at <freeze> (FROZENCFG); a claim file that is absent at the freeze makes both counters refuse
files.produced_by: L1, from CLAIMS-DRAFT.md plus the counters' own leg tables (see legcount)

files.why: the Ca counter grades LEDGER/BASEMISMATCH/REPAIR/ANNOTATE/RECEPTS off this file; the draft claim Ca requires >= 10 unique argv-executable pairs frozen here
files.produced_by: L1 from the wave-1 ScoutLedger/ExecAdaptCa work plus the L1's own verification

files.why: the C grader; its LEGS table is the authority the frozen claims.json legs[] must equal (LEGCOUNT)
files.produced_by: counter author seat, installed by the L1 at the freeze

files.why: the Ca grader; its REQUIRED_LEGS table is the authority the frozen claims.json Ca legs[] must equal (LEGCOUNT)
files.produced_by: counter author seat, installed by the L1 at the freeze

files.why: round-76 accept-c.py drives this file for the EVIDENCE leg (its own header names it); an uncommitted driver makes the evidence receipts unreproducible at <lands>
files.produced_by: counter author seat (round-76 counters/capture-evidence.py is the read-only pattern)

files.why: generates the J-series junk landings named by both claims' do-nothing controls; without it the junk receipts cannot be re-run at the freeze
files.produced_by: counter author seat (round-76 counters/junk-fixtures.py is the read-only pattern)

files.why: one used-by cell edit on a pre-existing row must keep APPENDONLY green; the claim Ca kill rule says a green exemption must not fire off a rule-2 cell
files.produced_by: copy of the round-76 fixture shape, re-labelled for round 77 by the counter author

files.why: a teaches-cell edit must fail APPENDONLY; the red half of the exemption pair has to be committed with the freeze or R1EXEMPT grades nothing
files.produced_by: copy of the round-76 fixture shape, re-labelled for round 77 by the counter author

files.why: records lands == freeze (data legs red, FROZENCFG green) and lands == base (refused, FAIL printed); the claim's do-nothing control is only met if this receipt exists at the freeze

legcount.rule: the legs[] list frozen in reports/round-77/claims.json must equal the counter's own leg table — same names, same order, duplicates included
legcount.authority: the counter source's module-level table literal: LEGS in accept-c.py, REQUIRED_LEGS in accept-ca.py; names are parsed with ast, never hand-typed, never imported
legcount.why_order_and_duplicates: both round-76 counters refuse exit 2 on a table mismatch and print `FAIL legs=0/N`; round 76's C table legitimately repeats INDEX at two positions, so a set-only comparison would miss a slot swap
legcount.blocker_on: any difference — the freeze must not be committed; reconcile by regenerating legs[] from the counter table (prose per slot), not by editing the counter to match a typed list unless the L1 decides the counter is wrong
